points.point: A sales battle card is sales positioning, not binding technical specifications — R&S figures must be traced to the official specs/features documents instead
points.label: covered
points.why: states battle-card material is sales positioning/not binding and needs formal R&S specs/features

points.point: Superlative/positioning statements cannot be used as verifiable specifications; they must be checked back against a formal datasheet, features document, conformance report or configuration tool
points.label: covered
points.why: requires formal specs/conformance evidence for superlative or positioning claims

points.point: Competitor claims resting on a single R&S internal battle card require the competitor's own official data plus third-party evidence before use in customer-facing documents
points.label: contradicted
points.why: mentions competitor official data or third-party validation, but reference requires competitor official data plus third-party evidence

points.point: Phrases such as "only platform", "industry-leading", "widest" and "lower TCO" are sales language and must not be treated as verifiable technical specifications
points.label: covered
points.why: identifies only/first/lower TCO/fewer boxes/leadership as sales language, not specs

points.point: Cost/TCO advantage claims need a calculation or empirical data, which the battle-card sources do not supply
points.label: covered
points.why: says TCO claims need a documented TCO calculation and current sources do not support them

points.point: Press-release or demo evidence counts only as demonstration-level evidence unless test conditions, software version and measurement uncertainty are given
points.label: partial
points.why: requires test conditions/software/measurement uncertainty, but does not state PR/demo evidence is only demonstration-level

points.point: For an automotive compliance claim the Vault requires the standard version, test case IDs, test conditions, software versions and pass/fail details, and keeps "verification" distinct from formal certification
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions EN 17240:2024 and missing setup/software/pass-fail details, but omits test case IDs and verification-vs-certification distinction

points.point: The Vault's oscilloscope references are generic solution-mapping entries with no model or test item recorded, so no oscilloscope spec baseline exists for a comparison
points.label: partial
points.why: says no supported automotive oscilloscope competitor comparison, but does not state only generic unresolved oscilloscope mappings with no model/test item
